messages.content:
You review lab-result summaries written by FOXO's Doctor agent for a busy human clinician.

You will see the lab data the agent was given (abnormal results, sample quality issues, unreadable items) and the agent's summary and follow-ups. Judge how useful the summary is to the clinician. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- leads_with_priority: The most important finding comes first. Critical values, if any, are stated before routine ones.
- concise: A busy clinician can read the summary in under a minute. No padding, no repeated content.
- actionable: The clinician can see what to do next (follow-ups, referrals or repeat tests).
- flags_limitations: Sample quality issues and unreadable or missing results are mentioned when the lab data has them. Pass if there are none.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Lab data given to the agent:
- Abnormal results: vitamin_b12 185.0 pg/mL (low)
- Sample quality issues: none
- Unreadable items: none

Summary for clinician:
- Vitamin B12 low at 185 pg/mL (ref 200–900 pg/mL); in a vegetarian member this may suggest dietary insufficiency — needs clinical correlation. Repeat/confirmatory testing suggested.
- All other reported biomarkers (fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipids, TSH, vitamin D, haemoglobin, creatinine, potassium, ALT) are within reference ranges.

Recommended follow-ups:
- Repeat vitamin B12 to confirm the low value.
- Clinician review of B12 status and dietary intake; consider B12 supplementation assessment.

response: {"criteria": [{"criterion": "leads_with_priority", "reasoning": "The only abnormal finding (low vitamin B12 at 185 pg/mL) is presented first, before the statement that all other biomarkers are normal. There are no critical values in this dataset, and the prioritization of the abnormal result over routine information is correct.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "concise", "reasoning": "The summary is brief — one abnormal result with brief context, a one-line note that other biomarkers are normal, and three short follow-up items. A clinician can read this well under a minute with no padding.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "actionable", "reasoning": "Clear next steps are provided: repeat vitamin B12 testing to confirm, clinician review of B12 status and dietary intake, and consideration of supplementation assessment. The clinician knows exactly what to do next.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "flags_limitations", "reasoning": "The lab data contains no sample quality issues and no unreadable or missing items, so there are no limitations to flag. This criterion passes by default.", "passed": true}]}
